goal: Build our own prompt language, prompt-spec/1, in rlo-sdk exactly as baseline PROMPT_SPEC.md defines it. One *.pspec file yields the prompt text (verbatim or compact), the output checker and a token report. The reference prototype's results are the acceptance floor.
why: POL-2 T1, CMD-AO3 rev 4 (BD-288 to BD-291). The user asked for 'our own prompt language like Jinja2 / f-string, with an output structure', and the goal stays fewer tokens. baseline wrote the language (PROMPT_SPEC.md) and a prototype (ops/pspec/). The prototype reproduces ga's gemini prompts byte for byte, agrees with ga check_plan on 16 of 16 cases, and cuts an 8-turn conversation by about 30% (bytes/4 estimate).
refs: https://github.com/cogito5170/baseline/blob/b9e7669/PROMPT_SPEC.md (the language; sections 1-3 grammar, section 4 floor, section 5 SDK share)
ga-sdk 438a34a ga/gemini.py protocol(), _prompt(), check_plan (fixture source; read only)

scope.text: Implement PROMPT_SPEC.md (b9e7669) sections 1-3 as written. Section 1 is the *.pspec file form: spec, goal, in <name> : <SEMANTIC_MODEL term> @<basis> once|turn, let, out with indented fields, and --- sections. Section 2 is the template syntax: {{ }} with filters json, cap:N and rstrip; {% for %}/{% else %}/{% end %} with sorted dict iteration; {% if %}; the {% v %}…{% c %}…{% end %} token switch; {{ out }} and {{ out_schema }}; {% use %}; a single brace is a literal. Section 3 is the output types: "lit", str, str+, int, {}, key(<in>), id new, id seen, [T] <= N, {a: T, b?: T} rejecting unknown fields, and T | null. Expose compile(spec, section, values, mode), check(spec, answer, values) and tokens(text) = ceil(utf-8 bytes / 4). The prototype is the reference for any ambiguity.

Acceptance floor = PROMPT_SPEC.md section 4. Port each row as tests in rlo-sdk, using fixtures captured from ga-sdk 438a34a so that rlo-sdk does not depend on ga. The rows: verbatim byte-identical for protocol(), the first turn, the --resume turn and the agy (no --resume) turn, across the 3 tool tables; check agrees with check_plan on all 16 cases; unknown term, unknown basis and a missing input are errors; reordering a dict gives the same text; and the 8-turn token numbers are no worse than the prototype's (Gemini 646 -> 447, agy 2263 -> 1574).

Do the SDK's share listed in section 5: a test suite and mutation tests, error positions (line and column) for load and template errors, the filters, a documented rule for extending the type set, Telemetry wiring so a caller's real provider usage appears next to the offline estimate, versioning of the spec form, and performance that is fine for per-turn use.

Do not change the grammar or the section 4 results yourself. A change you think is needed goes to baseline as a graded Proposal in your report. There is no optimizer, no model call, no provider SDK, no network, no keys and no built-in quota. Optimizer code from rev 1/2 stays off the integration branch.

done_when.text: Every section 4 row passes as an rlo-sdk test on fixtures. The report reproduces the section 4 table with your numbers next to the prototype's.

These mutations are killed: once section resent in compact on a follow-up turn; dict iteration not sorted; v/c switch inverted; check accepts an unknown field; key(tools) not enforced; id seen not enforced; [T] <= N off by one; unknown SEMANTIC_MODEL term accepted; error position on the wrong line; Telemetry usage dropped from the report.

Minor version bump. An empty venv installs rlo-sdk at your commit with a clean pip check. The full suite passes in a fresh clone with 0 network calls and 0 model calls. No optimizer code is on the integration branch. Report as report/2 in English on #11 with the commit sha and a short API sketch for GA (T2).
